new_issues.title: sq stats reviews counts every frontmatter-bearing .md in the reviews directory as a review, including resolution artifacts.
new_issues.why: reviews_usage_report globs *.md in reviews_dir and makes a row for every file with readable frontmatter and no runId; it never checks docType or the -review. filename segment. save_resolution writes {index}-resolution.*.md with docType resolution and a slice key into the same REVIEWS_DIR, so each resolution appears as a review row with an empty usage record (and matches --slice by name and index), inflating the review count and the unpriced denominator.

new_issues.title: sq stats run passes the raw run_id argument into the state path, so path-shaped ids can read .json files outside the runs directory.
new_issues.why: stats_run passes run_id to run_usage_report/StateManager, whose _state_path joins state_file_name(run_id) = f'{run_id}.json' to runs_dir without validation, so '../x' or an absolute path escapes. True, but this is a local CLI reading files the invoking user can already read; there is no privilege boundary, and state_file_name/_state_path predate the diff. Speculative hardening.
